transcripts.text: And a very, very happy Tuesday. Early Tuesday afternoon to you. How was your long weekend? Did you get a long weekend? And are you adapting to daylight saving? I must admit, I'm sure I'm not alone. It takes me about a week to get used to the change in the time. But anyhow, it is a Tuesday, as I mentioned. You're listening to 94.5 FM. That's FBI radio. We've played two songs already on the Wild Card show. Stuart Coop is my name, and I'm going to be with you till 1 o'clock this afternoon. Big thanks to August for a terrific morning show. August joining you again at 10 o'clock next Tuesday. And, of course, a big shout-out to Sabine for a terrific Up For It earlier this morning. Tomorrow, it's Wednesday, the morning show. We'll be at 10am and Ben Hanson will be keeping you company, playing tunes and having a chat with you. Now this is wildcard number 385. If you listen regularly you know the drill. We start off with a contemporary Australian song or artist and then we riff off that till one o'clock. We have real connections, imagined connections, requests from you and complete and utter wildcards. This week we're going to edge into a theme suggested by at least one of my wildcards. We're going to play a whole bunch of tunes that had nothing to do with that at all. Something new from Melbourne artists, which I like. I like her a lot. Koo Gondish Australian based in Sydney. New song from Katie Reid called It Doesn't Count When It's Your Friends. There you go. All right, let's go. Feet songs. When I suggested this a couple of weeks ago, Mark in Miranda quickly texted saying, what about Jack Johnson with Bubble Toes? So let's get underway with that one.

A rather obvious but an absolutely wonderfully, perfectly constructed pop song. It is 20 minutes after 12 on a Tuesday afternoon. You're listening to FBi and the Wildcard Radio Show with me, Stuart Coupe. We are celebrating songs referencing feet and walking. So if you've got songs that you like that fit into that category, send me a text 0435 123 945. 0435 123 945 You might also want to suggest some other themes for future wildcards I've had someone saying what about one about dogs What about one about cats So if you've got a contribution Or you'd just like to request a tune to hear on the show in coming weeks 0435 123 945 And the three tunes we listened to there First one was a suggestion from Mark in Miranda Jack Johnson doing Bubble Toes Then we followed that with the fabulously wonderful Nick Cave and the Bad Seeds song, 15 Feet of Pure White Snow. And then that classic from Crowded House, Fall at Your Feet. As I say, 0435123945, let's continue with feet songs. They're coming to Australia really soon. A bunch of people I know are excited. We're talking about the Ezra Collective. We're going to listen to them joined by Jasmine Lacey on God Gave Me Feet. What did he give you feet for? He gave you feet for dancing.

Ah, three fabulous feet-related songs on Wildcard and there's more to come. Don't worry about that. And a bunch of suggestions from you too. Some of them I'll get to now. Therese in Danger Island said, what about Boots Are Made for Walking by Nancy Sinatra and Walking in Memphis by Mark Cohen. And Therese suggested a colours theme, songs that mention colours. That's a good idea. I like that. Mark in Miranda, not going feet or colours, but wondered if I could play Active Affection by the wonderful Wailing Souls from their great album Firehouse Rock. Simon in Chatswood was down at Yours and Al's at the weekend. He saw Nice Biscuit and that made him think what about food-themed songs? And he wondered if I could play The Star by Nice Biscuit and he also said this weekend, speaking of food, He's going to see a banana. I think there was another bit to banana. I'll have a look in a minute. But then Kate said, what about Hothouse Flowers doing feet on the ground? I can feel another feet wildcard coming on. An anonymous texter said, Captain Matchbox, a whoopee band, your feet's too big. And I can see the texter coming in. So I'll get to the rest of those in the next mic break. But the three songs that we listen to first up, the Ezra Collective, who are coming to Australia soon with Jasmine Lacey doing God Gave Me Feet for Dancing. Then Ziggy Alberts with Four Feet in the Forest. And of course, that classic song from Patti Smith, Dancing Barefoot. Let us move on now with foot songs from the sublime to the look. this is the sort of, this is the radio show on FBI, which wouldn't even blink at the thought of playing Kenny Loggins. When I first mooted this theme of Feet Songs, Scott in Riverwood said, you've got to play this tune. And of course I went, you know what, we do.

And three more feet-related tunes on Wildcard this Tuesday afternoon on FBi Radio. A suggestion from Scott in Riverwood, Kenny Loggins doing Footloose, which prompted Paul and Annandale to go barefooting beats Footloose any time. After that, Spacey Jane with Cold Feet. And then that classic tune, which was sort of presented itself as an obvious one for a show on walking and feet. Lou Reed with A Walk on the Wild Side. Therese from Dangar Island texted in saying that she saw Suzanne Vega a couple of weeks ago at the Sydney Opera House. And she did a fantastic interpretation of A Walk on the Wild Side. I heard from Trina who'd like to request a shit list by L7. Nothing to do with feet, I don't think, but I'll go and check that one out and maybe bring that in for Wildcard next week. Donald in Willoughby, how are you doing? Donald said, walk like an Egyptian, one step beyond and just keep walking. And Joey said, walk and don't look back. Great song by Peter Tosh. Joey said he was at Yours and Al's in Wollongong at the weekend as well. And he and his wife saw 17 bands in 10 hours. That is impressive. Well done, Joey. And the day finished with them watching the drones, which is a mighty fine way to finish any day, I would have thought. 0435 123 945. If you've got requests, feet songs, foot songs, walking songs, theme suggestions, anything at all. We're going to leave the theme side of things alone. Only got time for a couple more tunes before the lunch program. We're going to listen to a new song called Worship the Flora from Ruby Archer. Peter Archer from the great band Crow was her uncle, Peter Archer, passed away just before the release of the new final Crow album, which is going to be, the album's called Hold Sway. It's going to be launched on October the 17th at the Marrickville Bowling Club and Ruby Archer is going to be performing on the night. Let's have a listen to her song, Worship the Flora. 7-7 in my mind time 11-11

Two more tunes to bring us pretty much to the end of Wildcard this Tuesday afternoon. Ruby Archer with Worship the Flora and, as I mentioned earlier, Ruby Archer playing with Crow to celebrate their Hold Sway album and the life of Peter Archer, Marrickville Biling Club, on October the 17th. We follow that with Steve Earle doing Guitar Town, the title track from his landmark album, which was released 40 years ago. And to celebrate that, the likes of Shane Nicholson, Duncan Phillips, Coppelline, Dave Favis, Katie Brianna and Adam Young are all getting together to perform songs from that record at the Merrickville Bolo again on October the 9th, which is this Friday. A bunch of texts came in. Kate said, what about if we're going to do Colours? Purple by Big Scary. Thank you, Kate. Angie says, Guilty Feet by Alana Stone. Brendan in Kellyville, Walk All Over You by ACDC. Maybe we're going to have part two of feet, foot, walking songs. But I'm going to leave you. Cappy's coming in in just a minute with the lunch program, so do stay tuned to FBI Radio. Stuart keeps my name. I'll be back next Tuesday at midday. Who knows? Will we have a theme? Will we just have wild cards? Will we just have requests? tune in and find out I'm going to leave you with a band from Melbourne called The Seven Ups and they've got this terrific piece called Lossless thanks for listening, see ya
